synopsis: Adding automatic braking changes an awareness-only system into a motion-controlling safety function within ISO 19014-2; matching the old warning system is therefore the wrong acceptance target, and braking targets must come from hazard analysis [f2075, f11986, f11989]. The safety case should separately analyze failure to intervene when required and intervention when unsafe or unnecessary, with separate acceptance thresholds [f2141, f11987]. Validation needs evidence for control hardware, software and environmental qualification beyond perception testing, and even perfect sensor simulation cannot compensate for incorrect braking or machine-dynamics models [f1098, f7735, f5089]. Cybersecurity, configuration and updates become safety-relevant when software commands brakes, while ISO 19014-4 excludes cybersecurity and therefore requires separate coverage [f3664, f7488]. Field exposure alone cannot prove a rare-event safety function, and the corpus found no published quantified reductions in physical testing for off-road safety functions [f312, f7563, f7865]. Planning remains qualified by standards described as draft, under revision or under publication in October 2026, unresolved machine-specific applicability, and disagreement over excluding machine learning versus assuring it within the safety function [f6547, f10419, f9786, f1125].
